name: Storybook
summary: A component workshop that indexes component stories, renders them in an isolated preview, and extends the manager/preview boundary with addons, controls, documentation, and test integrations.

features.name: Story definition contract
features.description: The fixed source contains CSF and story-shape tooling for discovering metadata and named story exports. Official documentation defines stories as component examples with args, parameters, decorators, and play functions that describe states and interactions.
benefits: Turns component states into named, reviewable artifacts
Provides metadata for rendering, documentation, and testing
costs: Story metadata and component contracts must remain compatible
A large story corpus increases indexing and maintenance work

features.name: Manager and preview separation
features.description: The fixed repository separates core-server, preview-api, manager-api, and rendering modules. The official architecture documentation describes the manager UI and preview iframe as distinct surfaces connected through Storybook's channel and configuration mechanisms.
benefits: Keeps authoring and navigation UI separate from component rendering
Allows preview rendering to run with framework-specific runtime configuration
costs: Cross-surface communication adds serialization and lifecycle contracts
Debugging requires reasoning about manager and preview state separately

features.name: Addon channel extension
features.description: The fixed type definitions expose addon APIs and manager/preview module boundaries, while the official addon documentation defines addons as extensions that can add panels, decorators, toolbars, and behavior through Storybook APIs and channels.
benefits: Adds capabilities without changing every renderer or story definition
Supports both manager UI and preview-side behavior
costs: Addon compatibility depends on public APIs and event contracts
Multiple addons can interact through shared manager and preview state

features.name: Indexed render and test workflow
features.description: Storybook's fixed core-server source includes story-index generation and the repository contains preview rendering and test integrations. Official documentation presents stories as inputs for interaction, visual, accessibility, and component tests through the Storybook test ecosystem.
benefits: Reuses one component-state artifact across development and verification
Makes rendered story identity available to tools and automation
costs: Test results depend on environment, renderer, and story setup fidelity
Indexing and rendering add build and runtime steps to component workflows

mathematical_views.question: How do component metadata, named stories, args, and decorators form a graph of renderable component states?
assumptions: A story is a labeled state-producing node
Metadata and decorators provide configuration edges

mathematical_views.question: Which state and commands cross the manager/preview boundary while a story is selected and rendered?
assumptions: Manager and preview are distinct runtime surfaces
Transport details and UI scheduling are abstracted

mathematical_views.question: Where can addon nodes attach to the manager, preview, story, and test surfaces?
assumptions: Addon APIs define extension points rather than arbitrary internal access
The graph does not assert historical influence among addons

benefits: Component states become reusable named artifacts
costs: Story metadata and component APIs must stay aligned

benefits: UI and rendering concerns can evolve independently
Optional capabilities can attach through public extension points
costs: Addon ordering and compatibility remain integration work

benefits: The same indexed story can support development and verification
costs: Indexing and environment fidelity affect test cost and confidence
